name: not belonging
description: A perception that your situation is uncomfortable and/or unwelcoming, but you have nowhere else to go.
perceptions: I don't seem to belong anywhere.
I don't have a place in society to call my own.
results: Depending on the situation, you may have negative feelings about others or yourself.

guidance.description: How to Create More Belonging for Yourself and Others -- There are small things we can do in our everyday lives to feel accepted and valued, and to help others feel the same.

examples: Couch surfing at a friends place.

variations.name: homeless
variations.description: Having no space that you can call your own, return to often, or keep your stuff.
perceptions: I don't seem to belong anywhere.
I don't have a physical place to call my own.
results: You may have negative feelings about others and/or yourself.

guidance.description: If you're interested in helping homeless people in your area, consider a local web search.

variations.name: spiritually homeless
variations.description: Desiring a situation that speaks to your deepest existential self, but sensing that you lack such a space.
perceptions: I can't find a spiritual community I'm comfortable with.
I think there should be a group that would fit.

guidance.description: As Americans leave organized religion, alternatives on the rise

variations.name: culturally homeless
variations.description: A sense that you don't fully belong in any particular place, being unaligned with others on language, food, manners, beliefs, or other social aspects.
perceptions: I sort of belong to multiple different cultural spaces.
But I'm not strongly aligned with any of them.
I don't have a place in society that is a clear fit.
results: Depending on the situation, you may have negative feelings about others or yourself.

guidance.description: A Simple Way To Find Out Where You Really Belong

commentaries.quote: When you've never felt like you really belonged somewhere, it's almost impossible to know what it will feel like to finally feel at home.
They are so caught up in their happiness that they don't realize I'm not really a part of it. I am wandering along the periphery.
Nomadic people have a broader view of 'home' than those of us that put roots down in one place for a long time. They feel welcome across a much bigger landscape
People who are homeless are not social inadequates. They are people without homes.
Sometimes we feel we straddle two cultures; at other times, that we fall between two stools.
